The suite itself is kept untouched as the control frame (vignette dosed in PIL only) and passed as a second image reference so the model matches a real photograph's tonality instead of a description of one. Paired with the balcony, the consultation room and the bathroom vanity, where it belongs.

Where the reference shows a sunset, a sun in frame, an orange or night sky, or a lit lamp as the main light, replace it: the sky becomes pale hazy overcast daylight, the lamp goes off or barely glows, and the scene is re-lit by daylight from a window on one side; that is the one change to the picture's content that is allowed. Real rooms have bounce fill from walls and ceilings, so shadows are grey-brown and open, and whites stay white because nobody graded the hotel. Overcast daylight with wall bounce and a blown window removes the graded-render look; the organic gradient then sits only where the light does not reach, anchored to the window, never a centred circle.

scene_methods.name: Lived-in Portra
scene_methods.why: The model stages exactly the props it is told and cleans every surface. One or two things nobody arranged (a pushed-back sheet, a glass leaving a water mark, a cable) plus a named film stock with its faults (handheld softness, slow shutter, lifted milky shadows) make it imitate a photograph instead of a render. The reference's light is not kept: it is replaced with side daylight, so sunset and night references get fixed rather than inherited. Halation, mixed lamp white balance, the named camera body and the pushed stop were removed as literal traps; border, date-stamp, grain-layer and glow-halo negatives are kept because the model has produced sprockets before.

scene_methods.name: Wide off-axis, deep focus
scene_methods.why: Render depth of field (a hard focus plane with uniformly creamy bokeh) and dead-centre composition are the two strongest AI tells after the spotlight. A wider lens, deeper focus, a slight tilt and an edge-cropped subject are how editorial travel photographers actually frame a room, and they leave empty wall or sky for copy. The reference's light is fully replaced so dark references are fixed, not preserved.

scene_methods.name: Phone candid
scene_methods.why: A casual small-sensor snapshot pulls the model to deep depth of field, mild HDR flatness, no creamy bokeh, casual tilt, no spotlight. It kills the CGI thin-lens and single-dramatic-key tells at once; the far side of the room sits in slightly noisy, HDR-lifted shadow, which is how a real phone shot of a dim room looks. Paired with the journey moments (airport, street, airplane window, entryway) rather than the suite.

scene_methods.name: Plain photo (control)
scene_methods.why: Every adjective becomes a rendered effect. A short prompt lets the model fall back on its photographic prior, which is more ordinary and therefore more believable than anything a mood block asks for. This is the control against which the other methods are judged, and the input for PIL grading when the parent doses the darkening numerically.

rationale: APPLIED. Dim templates: every mention of text removed ('calm and nearly empty', 'the middle of the frame is an even, empty darkness', purple: 'so the residual light and any pale surface read as neutral, never tinted'); reframed as a daylight/dusk photograph through a dark neutral filter, three stops under, brightest region a dark grey a third of the way to white, warm sepia-brown cast, vertical bottom-heavy falloff, 'ordinary focus' so the masters are sharp; purple blacks warm maroon-mauve, never blue; rim-light phrase restored. People edits: vignette-removal sentence inserted after 'Change only...'; the contradictory 'brighter on the lit side and nowhere else' resolved by splitting pale walls (flat, as E3) from dark walls (one smooth sideways shift, never darker in the corners); Light rewritten to the original side-lit key at eye level (user's 'go back to the original' wins over the above-front judge fix), slightly warm never orange, no 'north window'; Exposure rewritten so the wall keeps its true brightness and the face is exposed for its own skin; Colour rewritten with 'never lightened, never amber, deep brown stays deep'; skin/hair block replaced with 'exactly as in the reference ... same hairline, same density'; low_tint carries {TINT} (builder runs two people at 10 and two at 15, labelled 'tint 10%'/'tint 15%') plus the qualitative 'less than the eye normally notices' phrase; reading of Essos intensity: A-tier corners sit near 85-90% darker than centre, so 10-15% of that is a 9-13% corner drop, and the exact dose is a PIL asymmetric mask on the no-tint output (corner multiplier 0.85-0.90, central 60% untouched) whenever the model overshoots. people_purple: split-tone moved off the skin entirely (dark hair only where already near black, shadow side of clothing, shaded wall; light/grey hair keeps its colour; explicit no purple around eyes, nose or jaw); wall shade is a sideways shift not a band; shade warm not cool. new_person_t2i: editorial three-quarter or easy profile, 'never a clinical profile photograph', nose call-out deleted, skin block merged from both judges (pores, vellus hair, gentle colour variation across the cheeks, shine on forehead and cheekbones, expression lines appropriate to age, small natural asymmetries), no mole, no redness, 'no jewellery', gaze left to the briefs, 'clothing clearly separated in tone from the wall', full hairline, closing negative on redness/swelling/bruising/dressings. new_people: [1] hair cropped very short; PIL steps that guarantee the F1 density regardless of what the model returns: every dim and blur frame is multiplied by ~0.35 with the black point lifted to ~8 and checked for p95 luminance under 80/255 with cream #EBE4D1 text at 16 px; a Gaussian series (radius 12 and 24) is also produced from each sharp dim master and re-dimmed the same way, so the blur set exists even if the generated blurs disappoint. REJECTED. (1) Above-front key with a half-stop ratio for people: the user asked to go back to the original, which is side-lit at eye level with a stop or more of falloff, so the original-light fix wins. (2) 'Corners exactly as bright as the middle' on every wall: kept for pale colours only, because E3 and the originals show a gentle side gradient on dark walls and forcing flatness there fights the reference. (3) 'Thinning a little at the crown' for the Korean man: it draws hair loss on an AI person for a hair-transplant brand, the same rule that removed the Latino man's recession. (4) Mauve in the eye sockets, under the jaw and on the shadow side of the face (the softer purple fix): the stricter fix wins because on a rhinoplasty account that reads as bruising. (5) 'A mole or two' and 'patchy redness': redness on the nose reads post-op and the model over-delivers named flaws; moles were dropped for the same reason on the scalp line. (6) Dropping the dim corridor entirely: rewritten instead so the set keeps ten frames and the purple indices stay stable. (7) Making low-tint PIL-only: the user asked to experiment with a couple, so two generated strengths run and PIL remains the precise fallback.
